chapter_title: Concerning the Five Forms that exist in the Rulers
spiritual_reading:
Consider the ruling principle that governs every perverted affection and every falsity that rises from denial of good. Within that ruling principle there is a sufficient series of fundamental modes, patterned after the complete set of perversions that arise through the degrees of that infernal order.

In its highest part there is the domination of self-love, for it takes its determination from the ardor of corrupt love. In what should serve discernment and elevation there is instead the pride of reasoning and the soaring persuasion that comes from unstable and restless thought. In its operative powers and in its ultimates there is the cruelty of destructive desires, for its actions are formed from obscured understanding and from falsities that thicken into consent. In its inmost appetite there is the devouring falsity that swallows every perception of good and truth, for it draws from active denial. In its last extension there is the falsified truth that has been severed from life and turned into mere knowledge serving evil. These five modes are within that ruling principle, and they proceed from the complete set of perverted formations in that infernal domain.

Whenever it wills, it can act from its ultimates alone and thus move by gross falsities that serve evil. Whenever it wills, it can also act by a fuller complement of forces, bringing its interior and exterior powers into agreement for assault, and then it burns with the vehemence of corrupted love. Whenever it wills, it can lift its thought into airy persuasion and operate by subtle reasoning that seems to rise above what is merely natural. Whenever it wills, it can immerse itself in falsified truths and reason from them as though they were living, as those do who love falsity for its own sake. Again, whenever it wills, it can abase itself into mere denial and cling to it with appetite, reasoning from darkness as though darkness were wisdom. These modes are within it.

There are also three other qualities within it, but the first is unclear in the damaged text; it appears to concern the ordering or deployment of its powers.

The second is its skill in deceptive persuasion: whenever it wills, it can withdraw its influence so that its subordinate falsities do not perceive what governs them, and whenever it wills, it can disclose itself to them and by that disclosure compel them, and it can inflict spiritual death by its persuasive arts. Whatever it then affirms as truth, it can make effective with a kind of enchanted authority, because it speaks from the united force of evil and falsity.

The third is its hard resistance to any reformation from subordinate falsities: its structure is fixed in stubborn selfhood so that the assaults of lesser evils and lesser falsities cannot break it. No merely external strength of the natural mind can equal this resistance or overturn it, because it was brought into fixed form from the unyielding counsel of the selfhood that claims all things as its own, which is the generative source of destructive desires and their persuasions.

Again, there are three others within it.

Whenever it wills, the ardor of corrupt love flares up and its whole state becomes as though nothing but that ardor were present.

Also, whenever it wills, it can emit a contrary coldness, and its whole state becomes a total lack of charity, as though all love had been extinguished.

The third is its limited perception of those who serve it: while its subordinate falsities are in its immediate presence and under its dominion, it can perceive their intentions and discern the quality of their inner thought from what they present outwardly. But when they withdraw from its immediate sphere and separate themselves, it no longer perceives what they intend inwardly. There is no genuine spiritual life in it at all; what appears as life is only the agitation of anger and the fear of losing dominion that shows itself in its outward state. It is directed toward the destruction that it continually sets before itself as its goal.

fills.notes: The sentence contrasts walking on two feet with the world of smoke; the oldest-layer pattern is: manner “like the children of X” then the named world. This keeps the fivefold correspondence series intact (smoke as ultimates).

The next clause begins “four … on his hands and feet … like the children of fire”; the missing verb should introduce the shift from two-foot walking to fourfold motion using hands and feet together. “crawl on his” preserves the natural-image logic of quadrupedal motion as a mode he can assume at will.
Completes the quadruped description: “four feet” as hands and feet together. The following phrase “on his hands and feet” then specifies the fourfold ultimates.

The close of the clause must match “like the children of fire”; the governing correspondence in this section is that each mode not only moves but takes on the proper activity of its world. “burn” fits the fire-world activity in the oldest register better than moralized terms.

The spiritual translation indicates this damaged quality concerns ordering or deployment of subordinate powers. An impersonal, technical verb (“marshal”) matches the substrate’s cosmological mechanics rather than exhortation.
Completes the first quality as a statement of governance: the ruler can arrange his powers in ordered ranks. The clause is kept brief to avoid importing later institutional phrasing.

The line requires a capability statement introducing the arts of deception: “Shall a … his magic arts.” The spiritual sense is concealment and disclosure. “man conceal by” yields a coherent oldest-layer instruction-like description without Christian overlay.
Replaces the editor’s bracketed phrase with a more substrate-neutral verbal form. The function is effective utterance as operative enchantment; “work magic” expresses that directly.
Bridges “His body is strong, al … nails and claws … are not able” into a purpose-result clause. This matches the correspondential point: invulnerability to subordinate assaults.

Completes “No iron nor copper body will equal him … ; they will not be able to destroy him,” by specifying the comparison domain (strength). Keeps the natural-image register (metals, bodies) rather than moral terms.
The fire-quality is total assimilation: “entire body be made like the substance of fire.” This matches the spiritual translation: the whole state becomes as though only ardor were present.
Parallelism with ¶9: “freezes like a body of snow.” The image is not meteorological but total-state correspondence (coldness as privation).

The closing sentence must express fixed orientation toward destruction as a continually-presented end. “set before him” matches the spiritual translation (“sets before itself as its goal”) while keeping the impersonal, mechanical style.
Completes “established before him” in the final clause; the sense is the destruction fixed as an objective in his sight.

assessment: Most lacunae fall into tightly patterned fivefold and threefold series (modes of motion, elemental states, concealment-disclosure, invulnerability), which constrains the restorations. The first quality in ¶5 and the broken capability statement in ¶6 remain the least determinate; the fills there are correspondentially fitting (ordering powers; concealment by arts) but textually more uncertain than the parallel elemental clauses.
